title: മൂത്രം വഴി ഉള്ളിൽ കയറും കാണ്ടിരു! Candiru: Myth or Nightmare? Truth About the Penis-Fish! കാണ്ടിരു
description:
The Candiru (Vandellia cirrhosa) is one of the most feared creatures in the Amazon River. This tiny parasitic fish, often called the “vampire fish,” has inspired terrifying stories for generations. But how much of it is true? Is the candiru really capable of entering the human body? How does it find its host? And why do scientists around the world still study this mysterious species?

In this video, we explore:

✔️ The real biology and behaviour of the candiru
✔️ How it parasitizes other fish using its razor-sharp spines
✔️ Myths vs scientific facts about attacks on humans
✔️ How Amazon tribes protect themselves
✔️ Documented medical cases & scientific explanations
✔️ The truth behind urine-tracking myths
✔️ Amazing survival adaptations of this tiny predator

The only way to save life before the fish reaches the top is to take a fishhook and remove the penis. It is said that this is one of these fish. In the travelogues of European travelers in South America, it is recorded that many young men had to have their penis amputated due to accidents caused by this fish entering inside . We have heard many colorful stories about the bloodthirsty piranhas found in the rivers of South America. Like piranhas, the canduru or Lincolnrappan candiru is another terrifying fish that was once associated with the Amazon River. Welcome to today's video. Even today, if you search for "kandiru" on many YouTube channels, you will see videos telling stories of horrific attacks by this fish. Known as the penis fish or the blood- sucking vampire fish, many tribes in South America are still afraid of this fish and are afraid to go into the rivers because they believe that it will enter through their penises. No wonder, even in 2025, porcupines still believe that they will be able to remove their spines and stick them into other people's bodies. Many of us have scientifically proven that porcupines do not have such an ability. Similarly, the story of the Eka Canduru is not like piranhas, surrounding us in groups and attacking us, biting and eating our flesh. Canduru fish like to burrow into the penises of men and women who go to the river to bathe, and suck blood from there. However, there is no complaint that they have entered the anus. Then some researchers investigated and came up with some theories about why they only enter the urethra. The smell of ammonia in the urinary tract attracts them, and the candiru fish, which is about the same length as a toothpick, is a bloodthirsty fish that has become world-famous or infamous. The word candiru is a word used to refer to many catfish belonging to this category, including the paratha catfish. Many studies have been conducted on the species Vantalia syrosa, also known as the pencil catfish or paratha catfish, and the parasitic catfish. They are commonly found in the Amazon River basins in countries such as Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, and Ecuador . They will live on the bottom where there is not much shallow water and where there is turbidity . This baby fish is a parasite. Parasites are organisms that live by sucking blood from the gills, the respiratory organs of larger fish. It swims alongside these large fish, quickly burrows into their gills, ingests blood within seconds, fills its stomach, and then emerges to rest. They have sensors on their heads that can detect the presence of ammonia, which is released through the gills of large fish. They use it to detect the presence of large catfish and the location of their gills . These bloodsuckers do not cause any major damage to the gills of fish during this bloodsucking. Often, large catfish do not even know that a person has drunk their blood. They think of us as if they have been bitten by a mosquito. Those that live by taking the blood of other animals as food are called hematophagous. Because they live by drinking only blood, they are called vampire bloodsuckers. They are also called pencil fish because they have a very long, slender body shape like pencils. They are usually small, up to four centimeters long, but some can grow up to an inch long. About 207 species of fish have been found in this genus so far, some of which are up to 16 inches long. Because of this very slender body shape, they can easily crawl inside the gills of other fish very quickly. They also have small, curved teeth in the field. Most importantly, they have a very small head, as well as a long stomach that swells when they drink blood. They have spines on their heads that curve backwards, helping them to stay there without falling off even if they climb into the gills of other fish. They will leave the area after about two minutes, filling their stomachs with blood from the gills. If they stay there for longer, there is a chance that other predators will catch and eat them. Their bodies are semi- translucent, meaning they cannot be recognized in slightly murky water. We can only see the murky water outside their bodies. Fish cannot see. Only when their intestines are full of blood, we can recognize the color of the blood inside the intestines and thus see the fish. In all the stories, this fish is the younger sibling of the piranha. Many colorful stories and superstitions about the canard were spread all over the world until the 19th century. For centuries, not only tribes in Bolivia, Brazil, Peru, and Ecuador, but also European travelers Those who left carried with them beliefs, myths, and stories about this fish called Kanduru . The first recorded case of this fish burrowing into the male penis was in 1829 by a German biologist named CFP Mon Martheus, who did not see it directly, but rather heard it from local villagers. He also noted that when people went into the river, they used to tie a thread around the tip of their penis for safety. He also wrote that various tribes in other places used various methods to protect their penises when going into the river. This means that many tribes in South America believed this to be true for centuries. In any case, he was convinced that this fish was attracted to the smell of male urine and burrowed into it. In 1855, a French naturalist named Francois Louis Laporte wrote about a warning given by healthy fishermen to never go into the river for any reason. Their belief is that one should not urinate, as if doing so would cause a fish to jump through the urinary tract and penetrate inside, but he himself has indicated in his report that this is pure nonsense. He had already commented that this leap is inconsistent with fluid mechanics and against the laws of physics. He says that a fish in the air cannot have the energy and speed to jump against this rapid flow of urine . There are some reports that some physicians there have dealt with some accidents that occurred after a snakebite entered their body. Interestingly, it was later revealed that there were no natural predators in the areas where such cases were reported, meaning that piranhas are likely to be the villains in such stories of genital mutilation. In later reported cases, it is only said that the fish that entered the female vagina instead of the male penis were removed. In fact, the hole inside the penis is so small that even a baby can't fit through it without growing. Therefore, the scientific world viewed this as just a myth. However, in 1997, a medical case emerged from Brazil, with accurate reports from a surgeon, claiming that a spider had been surgically removed from a human penis. The case is that when a 23-year-old young man urinated in the river from knee-deep water, a rhinoceros jumped in and entered his penis . Urology surgeon Anosar Samad claims to have removed the rhinoceros fish after a two-hour operation . He also preserved the removed candiru in formalin . The surgery was also captured on video. It was certainly the first report with accurate evidence . However, in 1999, American marine biologist Stephen Spott approached this surgeon to find out the truth. All the evidence was examined. He then compiled what he learned into a book called Candaru Life and the Legend of Blood-Sucking Catfishes. He scientifically proves that the case is a false claim by presenting every possibility. Long before this, experiments had shown that Kandrup had no particular interest in urine. The only thing they rely on for food is their sight, and the specimen he kept was 133.5 millimeters long and 11.5 millimeters in diameter, that is, more than 13 centimeters long.
